. 2.  Heard learned counsel for the parties.

3. Petitioner-Company in this writ petition assails the award dated 15.01.2015(Annexure-1) passed by learned Civil Judge (Sr.Divn.), Kamakhyanagar in L.A. Misc. Case No.111 of 2014 in a reference under Section 18 of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894 (for short, "The Act").
4.

Mr. Dash, learned counsel for the Petitioner-Company submits that the petitioner- Company is a "person interestered" as defined under Section 3(b) of the Act and is entitled for an opportunity of hearing in the matter.

Neither the Land Acquisition Collector nor the learned Court below, who adjudicated the reference under Section 18 of the Act, issued any notice to the petitioner affording the petitioner-Company an opportunity of hearing in the matter and hence, the impugned award under Annexure-1 is not sustainable.
Thus, he prays to set aside the same and to remand the matter to Referral Court for de novo adjudication of the dispute under Section 18 of the Act giving the petitioner an opportunity of hearing.
4. Learned Additional Government Advocate, refuting the contentions made by the petitioner-Company, submits that an appeal under Section 54 of the Act lies against the impugned award.
As such, the writ petition is not maintainable and hence the same is liable to be dismissed.

5. Learned counsel for the claimant-opposite party No.1 while supporting the submission made by learned counsel for the petitioner-Company, submits that the petitioner is entitled to an opportunity Angul Sukinda Railway Ltd vs Rohita Biswal & Others .....

6. A statutory appeal under Section 54 of the Act lies against an award under Section 18 of the Act,
but at the same time, a writ petition is maintainable under Article 226 of the Constitution against determination of the amount of compensation by the learned Land Acquisition Collector or by the Reference Court as held in U.P. Awas Evam Vikas Parishad vs. Gyan Devi(Dead) by L.Rs. and Ors.

entities.text: U.P. Awas Evam Vikas Parishad vs. Gyan Devi(Dead) by L.Rs. and Ors
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Reported in AIR 1995 SC 725.

In the instant case, the claimant concedes to the submission of Mr.
Dash to the effect that the petitioner is entitled to an opportunity of hearing for just adjudication of the reference under Section 18 of the Act.

7. In that view of the matter without delving into technicalities with regard to maintainability of the writ petition, we set aside the impugned award under Annexure-1 and remit the matter to the learned Civil Judge (Sr. Divn.), Kamakhyanagar for de novo adjudication of the LA Misc. Case No.111 of 2014 giving an opportunity of hearing to the parties including the petitioner.

It is further directed that the learned Civil Judge (Sr. Divn.), Kamakhyanagar shall do well to adjudicate the reference afresh as expeditiously as possible, preferably within a period of six months from the date of receipt of certified copy of the order.
Parties are directed to cooperate for early disposal of the reference.
8. With the aforesaid observation and direction, Writ Petition is disposed of.
